steps.name: Rupert
steps.text: The war's over, Woody. You're free. You can go back to Laterano, to that small house your parents left you, and plant roses in the front porch.

steps.name: Rupert
steps.text: Then, you can find a chapel nearby and paint them on its ceiling, so they can listen to the prayers of every visitor. That way, the sounds will drift you into a peaceful night of slumber.

steps.name: Rupert
steps.text: I found your gun in the warehouse, but... not his. Bring it back with you.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: What about you? Where are you headed?

steps.name: Rupert
steps.text: I'll stay here.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: In Columbia...? But the war's over.

steps.name: Rupert
steps.text: Your war may be over, Woody, but mine has only just begun.

spans.text: war may be over, Woody, but mine has only just begun.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Woody. Hey, Woody...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Are you alright?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: How long have I been out...

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Three days.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: The kids got pretty tense when they saw me injured, so they went a little overboard. You banged your head on the staircase when they shoved you to the ground, and were out like a light.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Where's Jessica? And the others...?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Don't worry, she's fine. And I've sent someone to escort Helena.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: My guess is she'll reach that casino unscathed in half a month. Then she'll launder all the money there before handing it to Sylvia, who's already waiting in the frontier.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: ...You aren't going to pursue them?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: I told you already. I only care about what's in the contract. The higher-ups asked me to tow the plate to the specified location and maintain order on the way.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: It doesn't say a thing about what happens off the plate, so I don't care either.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: I may be a cold-blooded monster, but even I don't like feeding on the flesh and blood of others.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: So what're you gonna do with me?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: I have a mansion in southern Columbia. Got a great, big greenhouse. Wonderful place.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: You could change your name and enjoy your golden years there. I'll make all the arrangements.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: You ever lived there?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Never. But that's what the real estate agent said.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: ...Thanks for the offer, but if there's one thing I know, it's you never trust a real estate agent.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: If you ain't turning me over to the courts, then I'm leaving.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: To find your friends?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: To find my family.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Your gun's on my desk. The last convoy to the frontier is in half a month.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: You could...

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Go ahead, take the call.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Would you like some tea, sir? Thank you so much for coming all this way.

steps.name: Travel-Stained Lawyer
steps.text: Uh, thanks, Miss Brynley. Your family paid a lot of money to hire me, so naturally I'm at your beck and call.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Robbing a bank is a serious crime... It's going to be tough to win this, isn't it?

steps.name: Travel-Stained Lawyer
steps.text: Depends on what outcome you're hoping for.

steps.name: Travel-Stained Lawyer
steps.text: If you don't mind prison, we can get you the shortest possible sentence in the most comfortable environment, and once you're released, your record will be clean. No one will even remember.

steps.name: Travel-Stained Lawyer
steps.text: We do this all the time. It's nothing difficult, so long as you can afford it.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Okay. What else?

steps.name: Travel-Stained Lawyer
steps.text: Of course, not a lot of people enjoy the sights of a prison cell. We have an alternate plan for you. You could stay home under house arrest, or even go on vacation at some villa with a great view.

steps.name: Travel-Stained Lawyer
steps.text: Under supervision, of course.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Would that be difficult for you?

steps.name: Travel-Stained Lawyer
steps.text: Yes, but not especially so.

steps.name: Travel-Stained Lawyer
steps.text: If you don't want to spend a day in prison, and would rather go back to a normal life right away, like nothing ever happened... That would be quite difficult, but not impossible.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: ...In Columbia, aren't most criminals sent to the frontier instead of prison?

steps.name: Travel-Stained Lawyer
steps.text: Don't worry, Miss Brynley. With us on the case, things won't get nearly that dire.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: No... I'm saying that's what I want.

steps.name: Travel-Stained Lawyer
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I should be out there. I broke the law, and that's the price I should pay.

steps.name: Travel-Stained Lawyer
steps.text: And you expect me to tell that to your father? Personally speaking, that's probably the most difficult thing you could ask of me.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: No... the most difficult thing would be to try and stop me.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Because that's outright impossible.

steps.name: Travel-Stained Lawyer
steps.text: You're... pretty determined.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: You're right, I am. More than I've ever been.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Not taking the call?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: I've never told anyone, but I hate phone calls. Loathe them.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I can tell. With that frown, you could hold a piece of paper between your eyebrows.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Is it that obvious?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Yeah...

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: But yes, every time my phone rings, I have to suppress the urge to draw my gun and shoot the damn thing.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: I've thought about it so, so many times, but every time I've managed to swallow it and answer.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: It's just a phone...

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Try spending two months with it on the battlefield. It changes everything.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: You're on call from sundown to sunup. When you pick it up and the voice says, 'attack,' you've no choice but to obey and send your men charging into enemy lines.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Then, you fight from sunup to sundown. You bring back everyone you have left, but before you even have time to catch a breather, the phone rings again.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: The voice says, 'hold the line,' and you have to send everyone back to the frontlines to keep fighting a never-ending battle.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Let's part ways here, Woody. If I lost my right to give a eulogy at your funeral years ago, then I hope you'll at least hear out my last request.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I'm listening.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Don't die in someplace I've never even heard of.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: ...Fine. I have some parting words for you, too.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Yeah?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: If you can't go back to how things were, you can at least hang up and call back later. Don't let them force you to keep your eye on it.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: I hope you'll always remember this phone call.
He picks up the phone on the desk and punches in a few numbers

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Is this the president of the bank? Hello, sir. I was a little busy, and couldn't answer your call.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Right, we ran into some trouble during the towing. I understand your frustration, but to me, as long as the plate reaches its destination, the mission will be a success.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Everything else is a sideshow. No one's going to care.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Right, I understand. The money is very important to you.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: I get that business has been on the rise, and the people from Trimounts could help you climb even higher. And now that the money's gone, my guess is they won't just let you off the hook.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Of course, I also realize you aren't worried about them. You're worried about the higher-ups, who are even harder to deal with and can truly decide your fate.

spans.text: Of course, I also realize you aren't worried about
. You're worried about the higher-ups, who are even harder to deal with and can truly decide your fate.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Yes, I understand. I understand all that.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: So, what do you say I help you fill in the hole? It's no small sum, but nothing I can't afford.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: In return, perhaps you could help me with a small favor.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: I have a few documents that I'd like you to sign for me. Under the table, as it were.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Someone's knocking on your door? Perfect, sounds like my mercs have arrived with the papers.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Haha... You're afraid to sign?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: But think of our partnership. This is a win-win.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: I'll give you another call in half an hour. I hope you'll have made your decision by then. Talk to you later.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Come in.

steps.name: Secretary
steps.text: Sir, the money is ready. We're just waiting for the bank's decision.

steps.name: Secretary
steps.text: But I must say... Taking over that platform in Bolívar took a whole lot less work than this one.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Well, that's Bolívar.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Bolívar doesn't have cutting edge scientists, nor any tech companies jostling for control of all the abandoned plates they can get.

steps.name: Secretary
steps.text: Not to mention the favorable prices for plates and ownership transfer procedures they have there.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: They wouldn't mind getting on our good side, after all.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Alright. No more complaining about things not going to plan.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: If peace is a string, then the tighter it's stretched, the more the ones holding the ends will want a knife to cut it with. But as soon as it's cut, you either get rid of the knife immediately, or hold onto it forever.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: We've been stretched too tight for too long, by someone much stronger than Bolívar.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Who knows how many more Davistowns we'll have to handle? I'd rather get the big guy to loosen his grip. Or even show him how much it hurts when the string snaps.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: But an old platform they wouldn't think twice about... Hm, this might be even more useful than we thought.

steps.name: Secretary
steps.text: If we consider only the immediate impact... the security of the surrounding areas could be greatly improved once we've established the training centers in Bolívar and Eastern Columbia.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Of course. If we didn't care about that, then what separates us from the guys who only know how to grease palms... No, what separates us from the 'big guys'?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Well, that's all a problem for the future.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: ...It's the bank president again. I suppose it wasn't a difficult decision.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Care to listen in?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: ...Why do we have to set sail now, of all times? I wanted to see Jessica and Woodrow off.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Stop whining and pack your clothes.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: You left them all over the floor... Tsk tsk.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: How come you two are so calm about this? Who knows if we'll ever see her again, once she's out on the frontier.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Mr. Cliff didn't approve her resignation. So even there, she'll still be a member of Blacksteel.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: What? B-But... She's going out there to serve her sentence...

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Yes, correct. But with her identity as a Blacksteel employee... and the job.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: ...The job?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Right. No matter where you go, you can never escape this job.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Maybe we'll get a mission in the frontier one day, and we'll get to see her.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Uh...

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Now hurry and pack your clothes.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: I... I can't believe you two were keeping this from me. I thought I'd never...

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Don't blame us. Blame Engineering for keeping you so busy that we never got a chance to talk.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Hm? What's this...?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Something wrong?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Oh, no. I just found a note in my pocket.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Big whoop. Call me when you find a blank check.
Half a month ago, Laura wore that coat while bidding her friend farewell with a hug.
She slipped a note into her friend's pocket, but didn't notice her friend doing the same.
Laura turns away from the other two and opens it up.
There are a few numbers and a sloppily scribbled message:
'If you ever need funding, give this number a call.'

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Another one.
Ma'am, you've been in this pub all night. The owner is about to close up.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: That's alright. I know the owner.
Are you waiting for someone?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Nah, I ain't never waited for no one my whole life.
Is someone waiting for you, then?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Yeah...
Will they get to meet you?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: I got a lot of people waiting for me, you'll have to narrow it down.
Let's not worry about the distant ones. The closest, waiting for you right now.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Yeah, of course they will. Gave 'em my word.
It's hard to find someone who takes promises so seriously these days. Here, let me treat you to a round.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: You tailed me this long just to buy me a drink?
...Believe it or not, I made a promise too. I promised the girl you're supposed to meet that she'll get to see you.
You can call me Tila.
In a swath of scorched earth, I see a spark light up and drift with the wind into the distance, before perishing into ashes.
Or perhaps it lit up the night sky and brought forth the daylight.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: You really plan on coming to the frontier with me?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: You know what it is you're throwing away?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I do.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: It's a stupid-ass choice.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Maybe in a few years, a few months, or even a few days... I'll come to think the same.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But I can only decide with the heart I have now.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: If I think it's worth a shot, there's no reason for me not to act.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: You think you'll find what you're after out there?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Before... I always put all my effort into chasing things I could never reach.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: When I was a kid, I tried to chase my siblings, who were all taller than me. When I was a teenager and my grandfather died while I was out of the country, I rushed to attend the funeral I could never have made it to in time.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: And then, after I grew up... I chased disasters and conflicts I could never possibly stop. Again and again.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I'm always chasing, but I never make it in time.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But this is different. This time I'm not chasing anything.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Because I'll be there from the very beginning.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Then let's get going. Hope you're ready for a fresh start.

steps.name: Grandfather
steps.text: Why the tears, Jessica?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: My castle fell down. I spent all afternoon on it, but now there's nothing left.

steps.name: Grandfather
steps.text: Jessica, you built your castle on the beach. Of course it'll fall down when the waves come crashing.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I'm so dumb... Why didn't I build it somewhere safe...

steps.name: Grandfather
steps.text: What kind of nonsense is going through your silly little head? You're my granddaughter, how could you be dumb?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But my siblings are all so much smarter... They know all these things I don't...

steps.name: Grandfather
steps.text: They're adults. Of course they have more experience than you. When you grow up, you'll be just like them.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But won't they be even more amazing by then?

steps.name: Grandfather
steps.text: Huh... How come you have so many weird questions?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Sorry...

steps.name: Grandfather
steps.text: Now now, don't be so upset... How about I rebuild your sand castle with you?

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Will you really...? But even if we do... it'll still come crashing down because of the waves tomorrow.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: In the end... There still won't be anything left...

steps.name: Grandfather
steps.text: Jessica, if you're so worried about the waves wrecking your castle, how about we pick a beach further from the water, and rebuild it there?

steps.name: Grandfather
steps.text: Even when you lose everything, there's always the future... and we need to believe in it.

steps.name: Grandfather
steps.text: Don't be afraid to start over.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Yeah... Let's start over.
A warm hat is placed on the girl's head. Its brim is so wide, it covers almost her whole face.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: If you want to cry, cry. You've been through so much... Must be tough to bear.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I'm not...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Ain't nothing to be ashamed of, Jessica. New lives always start in tears.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: It's the very first step toward breathing.
After a long silence, a sob can be heard from under the hat.
The old man doesn't look down. Instead, he turns his gaze to the far end of the snowfield.
The sky beyond the horizon is dyed red by the dawn clouds, and its bright light reflects off the crystal-clear snow.
The vermillion hue stings his eyes with a sharp pain, and his tears begin to well up.
